title: Check your understanding: Recognizing Conflict Markers

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of recognizing conflict markers?
options: Conflict markers delimit sections that Git could not automatically combine. The developer must inspect both sides and any shared context, edit the desired final content, and remove the markers before staging the resolution.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: Conflict markers delimit sections that Git could not automatically combine. The developer must inspect both sides and any shared context, edit the desired final content, and remove the markers before staging the resolution.
questions.explanation: Conflict markers delimit sections that Git could not automatically combine. The developer must inspect both sides and any shared context, edit the desired final content, and remove the markers before staging the resolution.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with recognizing conflict markers?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
